title: OpenAI’s answer to Meta Muse is a cute AI agent that never clocks out
summary: The always-on AI agents can keep projects moving across your apps while you’re away.
body: TL;DR OpenAI’s new Dots are always-on AI agents that can keep working across connected apps even when you’re not actively chatting with them. A Dot can monitor ongoing work, suggest or complete next steps, and carry context across ChatGPT, Slack, and Teams. Dots are rolling out gradually to Pro, Business Premium, and Enterprise users in eligible markets. ChatGPT began as a place you opened when you needed an answer. Then ChatGPT Work pushed things further, taking on long-running jobs across apps and files. OpenAI’s next step is to make the AI stick around even after you close the chat. At DevDay 2026, the company unveiled Dots , always-on personal agents that can keep working toward your goals in the background. Powered by GPT-6 Astra , each Dot gets its own cloud computer and browser and can connect to more than 4,000 apps through OpenAI’s plugin ecosystem. OpenAI dresses them up as colorful, fuzzy characters you can name, but the idea goes deeper than a mascot. You can talk or message your Dot through ChatGPT, then reach the same agent through Slack or Microsoft Teams without losing context. Texting is coming soon.

title: Your next Google Play subscription could work very differently
summary: New tools also add bundles, team seats, and smarter payment recovery.
body: TL;DR Google Play is adding usage-based subscription billing aimed at AI apps and other services with variable costs. New options will also support team subscriptions, mixed subscription/one-time purchases, and cross-app bundles. Google is also testing smarter grace periods, cancellation discounts, cheaper-plan offers, and Play Store winback deals. Google Play’s billing story changed earlier this year when Google opened the door wider to alternative billing systems and external web payments, giving Android users more choice over how they pay. Now it is turning its attention to subscriptions that still run through Google Play itself, with new billing options that could make AI apps, bundles, and failed payments work very differently for users. In a blog post , Google says it is testing and rolling out several new subscription options, including Usage-Based Billing. The new system targets services with variable costs, such as generative AI apps , and it lets users maintain a prepaid balance that can automatically top up when it drops below a set threshold. That opens the door to billing tied to consumption rather than only a fixed recurring amount.

Amazon’s car-centric Alexa accessory, the Echo Auto, has vanished from active sale on Amazon, leaving buyers to wonder whether the hardware giant is quietly pulling the plug on its in-car dongle. title: TECNO and Angélica Dass Unveil “100 Portraits of Becoming” Gallery, a Global Portrait Project Bringing 100 Ways to See Humanity
summary: Beginning with 20 portraits from Kenya and followed by the Philippines, the five-country project advances inclusive imaging toward a deeper human understanding of the people behind the image, exploring different ways of seeing people and the individual stories that shape their lives.
body: Website of 100 Portraits of Becoming Credit: TECNO TECNO and internationally acclaimed visual artist Angélica Dass today unveiled the “100 Portraits of Becoming,” a two-year global portrait project spanning Kenya, the Philippines, Saudi Arabia, Türkiye and Brazil. Launching with the first 20 portraits and personal stories from Kenya, the project will ultimately bring together 100 individuals and 100 distinct stories of identity, choice, change and growth. It builds on TECNO’s long-term work in inclusive imaging, where truthful representation begins with ensuring that people across different skin tones can be rendered naturally, fairly and accurately.

title: Google has just teased Android 18, and here’s when we’ll learn more
summary: Android 18 just made a surprise cameo on Google's big stage.
body: TL;DR Google has officially mentioned Android 18 on the agenda for its upcoming Android Dev Summit 2026. The agenda teases “powerful new graphics features” for Android 18, giving us an early hint at what’s coming. Android Dev Summit runs October 28–29, with an Android leadership keynote that could reveal more about Android 18. We’re still months away from Android 18 landing on our phones, but Google has just given us the first taste of what’s coming. Google is bringing back its Android Dev Summit on October 28 and 29 , and while the event is primarily for developers, something on the agenda should interest the rest of us too: Android 18. The company has published the two-day schedule, and Android 18 appears alongside a tease of “powerful new graphics features.” Google isn’t telling us exactly what those features are yet, but this is one of the first official breadcrumbs we’ve received about the next major version of Android.

title: Samsung Browser can now hunt down coupons while you shop
summary: The browser can surface deals based on the site and items in your cart.
body: TL;DR Samsung Browser is rolling out its new Smart shopping feature. It can recommend coupons based on the shopping site you’re visiting and what’s in your cart. The feature is enabled by default in the latest Samsung Browser app, but you can switch it off in Settings. Samsung Browser has finally decided to put its coupon-hunting skills to work. Earlier this year, we dug into an unreleased browser build and found signs of a new Smart shopping feature designed to sniff out coupon codes and potentially shave a few dollars off your cart total. It wasn’t usable then, but that’s changing now, with Samsung rolling out the feature in the latest version of its Android browser. X user Kailash spotted Smart shopping rolling out with Samsung Browser version 30.0.5.24, a newer build than version 30.0.0.67 currently available through the Google Play Store. We were able to download and install the 30.0.5.24 APK, and sure enough, the Smart shopping option appeared under Settings > Useful features > Smart shopping .

title: This Meta Muse incident is a scary warning about trusting AI agents
summary: Convenience is great, until your AI starts making the arrangements.
body: TL;DR Meta’s Muse negotiated a Facebook Marketplace sale, shared the seller’s address, and arranged a pickup without him realizing someone was coming. Meta is investigating the incident, and it remains unclear whether Muse overstepped its permissions or acted on authorization it had already received. The incident highlights the risks of handing sensitive, real-world decisions to AI agents, especially when personal information or in-person interactions are involved. It’s only been a few days since Meta launched Muse, and we’re already getting a sense of how much Meta wants its new AI agent to do . But the more an AI can do for you, the more you also have to trust it with. One early Muse experience shows why that can get uncomfortable very quickly. Threads user Matt Robb shared what happened after using Muse to handle a Facebook Marketplace listing. According to screenshots he posted, the AI negotiated with a buyer, agreed to a price, shared his address, and arranged a pickup — all without him realizing someone had actually been invited over.
